items.title: David Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 18, 2003
items.q: Like this guy Manolito Simonet, he’s great. This guy’s got like a number two hit in Cuba. They don’t even hear about him up here.

ctx.x: That’s good. Good to have those kind of people in your back pocket.

Yeah but I’m trying to collect these people all over the world. It’s like, it’s not in New York where you find everybody. There’s other places where you find people like, it’s one of a kind. There’s a few people like that on this planet. And I’m trying to assemble them. That’s kind of what I’m trying to do. There’s some talents down in Cuba man, that is untouched, untapped. There’s a few great people, great bands, that people haven’t even heard. Like this guy Manolito Simonet, he’s great. This guy’s got like a…

I’m not sure if I can phrase this question but I’ll try. If I was to take a solo of yours and transcribe it, and then match what you’re playing against the chord structure and try to justify everything you’re playing by saying “notice how David took the tritone substitution,” and all that, would that be legitimate or are some of the things you do happy accidents?
